title: Iki action (iki/v1)
description: Something a plugin does to entities: compute properties, create new entities from them, or import them. Each run records what it read, what it wrote and where it ran.

^x-.description: A key for tools, such as `x-acme-reviewed`: kept in the file, ignored by Iki, and dropped from the build (ADR 0293).

apiVersion.description: The spec version this manifest follows.

name.description: The action's name in snake_case. Elsewhere it is `namespace/plugin.name`, such as `iki/protein.translate`.

inputs.description: The entities a run reads, by name. Leave it out for an action that imports or fetches entities.

params.description: The values a person (or an agent) chooses when they run it, by name.

effects.description: What a run may write. Its output is checked against these, and anything else is refused.

creates.description: The types of entity a run may create, each with how many and what they're derived from.

updates.description: The fields a run may set on its inputs' entities, by input.

runs_on.description: Where it runs: a compute tier and one of the plugin's environments.

environment.description: One of the plugin's environments, by name, such as `alphafold-gpu`.

lifecycle.description: For the container and vm tiers: a machine for each run (`ephemeral`, the default), or a warm pool (`persistent`).

resources.description: More than the environment's minimum, if this action needs it.

command.description: What the worker runs, as a list of arguments (no shell). Paths are relative to the plugin's root, or absolute inside its image.

deterministic.description: The same inputs and params always give the same results, so an earlier run's results can be reused.

checkpointable.description: It saves its progress in $IKI_CHECKPOINT_DIR, so an interrupted run resumes instead of starting again.

batchable.description: How many entities one job may handle at once, for quick actions with one input.

artifacts.description: Files a run writes besides its results, kept for people to download.

keep.description: Glob patterns, relative to the run's output directory.

retention.description: How long its artifacts are kept, such as `90d`: the deployment's default unless given, and never less than the deployment's minimum.

network.description: The hosts a run may reach. None by default: runs have no network access. `{settings.<name>}` is the host a deployment gives in that setting, which has `format: hostname`.

requires_settings.description: The plugin's settings a run needs, by name, such as `ncbi_email`: ones that are neither required nor have a default, so a deployment may leave them unset. Until it sets them, the action can't run there, and people see why before they launch it.

software.description: The tools its runs make entities with, by name and version, such as ImmuneBuilder 1.2: what its image or requirements install, for whoever reviews the plugin. Entities its runs create are recorded as made with them (ADR 0106). An action that only fetches or reads records lists none.

name.description: As its authors name it, such as `AlphaFold` or `RDKit`.

version.description: The release it runs, such as `2.3.2`.

metrics.description: The numbers its runs report about themselves (`metrics` in their output), by name, such as a score. A workflow's conditions can read those declared here.

additionalProperties.description: One metric, by the name its runs report it under in `metrics`.

secrets.description: Secrets a run needs, by name, such as `NCBI_API_KEY`. Each deployment keeps them in its secret manager, for this plugin alone; runs get them as environment variables, and their logs never show them.

required.description: Whether the action can run without it. Defaults to true.

description.description: For the administrators who set it: what it's for, and where to get one.

apis.description: The plugin's outside APIs its runs call (`apis` in plugin.yaml), by name, each with what a run sends it: people see it before they launch, and consent to it.

additionalProperties.description: One of the plugin's APIs, by its name in plugin.yaml, and what a run sends it.

sends.description: What of a run goes to the API: fields of its inputs' entities, and its params.

inputs.description: Each input's fields that are sent, such as `protein: [sequence]`.

additionalProperties.description: The fields of this input's entities that are sent.

timeout.description: The longest a run may take before it's stopped. Defaults to 1h; at most 7d.

retries.description: Which failed attempts are tried again, as a new job after a short backoff, and how many times.

max.description: How many times a run is retried, at most: 2 unless given, or 0 for an action with `network` or `apis`.

on.description: Which failures are retried. A run that ended in an error of its own isn't, unless `failed` is listed.

secret_name.description: A secret's name: the environment variable runs get it in, such as `NCBI_API_KEY`.

tier.description: `self_hosted`: a machine a compute admin registered for the project's team, such as an instrument's PC, a licensed workstation or an on-premises GPU, matched by its labels. `backend`: Iki's isolated worker pods. `container`: the plugin's image on Kubernetes. `vm`: a virtual machine, with GPUs if needed.

duration.description: A length of time, such as `90s`, `30m`, `8h` or `365d`.

constraint.description: The schema versions it works with, such as `>=2` or `>=2,<4`.

input.description: An input: the type of entity it takes, how many, and whether a run needs it.

type.description: The type of entity it takes; its subtypes are taken too.

max.description: With `many`: the most entities one run takes.

optional.description: A run can start without it. Otherwise whoever launches the run must choose its entities, and a workflow step or trigger must give them.

reads.description: The fields of its entities the run reads (ADR 0284): their values carry these, the fields their roles name, and the references `include` names, and no others. A field of the input's type, its own or a parent's. Left out, the run reads every field.

from_project.description: Not chosen by whoever launches the run: each run is given every record of its type that its project owns and hasn't archived, at their current revisions, such as a core's ranking of the projects it serves (ADR 0232). It takes many, at most its `max` and 1000; with none there, a run that needs it can't start.

include.description: Its type's references whose entities the run reads too, such as a structure's `chains`, or a list of rows' (ADR 0161), such as a complex's `components.part`: each one or list of them, at the revision it had when the run was launched, under each input entity's `included`. Whoever launches the run must be able to read them.

then.description: Files are the person's to choose: a list of files has no default, as a file has none.

type.description: `file`: a file the person uploads or chooses, such as one to import. The command finds it in input.json's `files`, by the ID in `params`.

required.description: The person must choose a value. A param with a default can't be required.

default.description: The value when the person doesn't choose one.

type.description: The type of entity it creates.

cardinality.description: `one` (the default): a run creates at most one, in output.json's `creates`. `many`: any number, in `creates` or a `creates_file`'s lines.

receive_into.description: Receive a fresh physical record with its starting amount into the container named by this single required input. Each inline create supplies its receipt.

match_on.description: One of the type's unique fields, such as a LIMS record's ID. A create whose value an entity in the run's project has already updates that entity instead, as a revision with its origin.

on_match.description: What a create that matches an entity on `match_on` does: `update` (the default) writes its values to that entity, as a revision; `keep` leaves the entity as whoever made it first made it, and the run gives it as the create's entity. `keep` is for a record only one of its makers may write, such as a result's impact case after a failed calibration, which a trace, an instrument use or Equipment QA may each open first.

derived_from.description: The inputs each created entity comes from, for its lineage.

input.description: The input whose entities it changes.

fields.description: The fields it sets on them.
